questions.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $15{x}_{1},$ where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{1},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{1}}{{q}_{1}\cdot {q}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 1+(-4)\cdot (-3)}{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2+12}{1+9} \\  & =\frac{7}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
15{x}_{1}=15\cdot \frac{7}{5}=21.
$$

questions.problem:
Given the **orthonormal** basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $2{x}_{2}$, where ${x}_{2}$ is the second component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{\sqrt{41}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{5}{\sqrt{41}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{\sqrt{41}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{4}{\sqrt{41}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{41} \\ -9 \\ -2\sqrt{41}\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing ${x}_{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =x\cdot {q}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{41} \\ -9 \\ -2\sqrt{41}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{\sqrt{41}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{4}{\sqrt{41}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-15+0-8 \\  & =-23.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
2{x}_{2}=2\cdot (-23)=-46.
$$

questions.problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis $B=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\}$ of ${R}^{2},$ find $[x]_{B}$ if $x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing the components of $x,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{6}{\sqrt{2}}=3\sqrt{2} \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=-\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{2} \\ -\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis $B=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]\}$ of ${R}^{2},$ find $[x]_{B}$ if $x=[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 10\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing the components of $x,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 10\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}]=-12+8=-4 \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 10\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]=16+6=22\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 22\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $\frac{5}{3}{x}_{1}$, where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\}\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 8\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{1},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{1}}{{q}_{1}\cdot {q}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 1+4\cdot 2+8\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2+8+8}{1+4+1} \\  & =\frac{18}{6} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{5}{3}{x}_{1}=\frac{5}{3}\cdot 3=5.
$$
